items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqwy: UN climate talks in Turkey (COP31) ended without a deal after the EU and Pacific island nations rejected a final text that didn't mention phasing out fossil fuels, while poorer nations wanted firmer funding promises to adapt to warming. It's the first such collapse since Copenhagen in 2009. Outgoing UN chief Antonio Guterres blamed fossil-fuel interests for stalling progress.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: Israeli forces have demolished several homes in the village of Zawtar ash-Sharqiyah in southern Lebanon, leveling buildings to the ground, as such demolitions continue amid ongoing tension between Israel and Lebanon.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n: A Russian navy corvette, the Merkury, sank after a suspected Ukrainian sea-drone strike while refueling at Benghazi, Libya, more than 1,000 miles from Ukraine. Two of several drones hit the ship, which had docked on its way home from a Mediterranean voyage. The attack shows Ukraine's drone navy, built from scratch during the war, reaching further than ever before.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/videos/cr1ewg: COP31 in Antalya, Turkey ended without agreement after the EU and other nations rejected a fourth draft deal that omitted a commitment to phase out fossil fuels. The EU accused oil-producing states of hijacking the talks, while Russia defended its opposition and criticized the EU. It became the longest-running UN climate summit, having overrun by two days.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2: WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called for peace after heavy fighting near a hospital in DR Congo's Ituri province, the center of an Ebola outbreak, disrupted the response effort. Health workers and aid staff had to shelter in a maternity ward for over 24 hours. The violence puts patients and responders at risk just as the outbreak needs uninterrupted care.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026: Powerful Pacific storms brought record-breaking waves to California's coast this week, with a buoy near Monterey recording a 34.1-foot wave, the highest in 30 years. Beaches and piers closed as warnings of 10-22 foot waves extended through the week. The same storm system caused record rain in San Francisco and knocked out power to 32,000 homes in Sacramento.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cr89: A suspected drone attack caused an explosion on a Russian navy ship docked at Benghazi, Libya at dawn on Sunday, Libya's eastern government said, with no casualties reported. A separate commercial vessel off Benghazi was also struck, injuring people lightly. Satellite images and US intelligence firm Vantor identified the targeted ship as the Russian corvette Merkury.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2: South Korea's Kospi index dropped as much as 3.7% on Monday, extending a tech-led sell-off across Asia and Wall Street. Japan's Nikkei and Taiwan's Taiex had already tumbled over 5% on Friday, while the Nasdaq fell 5.3%, wiping out its 2026 gains. Investors worry tech firms can't sustain their massive AI infrastructure spending.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/environment/: Environmentalists in South Africa are replanting five centuries-old baobab trees after an exporter dug them up without permits to ship them to an unnamed buyer in Georgia. The trees, stranded in a Durban warehouse since July, have been moved to a reserve in Timbavati to recover. A similar export to a Georgian billionaire's park happened in Kenya four years ago.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/videos/cre3dv: Several people were killed when a Russian strike hit a residential building in the village of Dymer in Ukraine's Kyiv region early Sunday; local officials said six people died and six were injured, with others still missing. Rescue efforts have been hampered by continued drone-attack warnings near the site, though some residents were evacuated earlier in the day.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/w: West Bengal BJP chief Samik Bhattacharya called for street protests over the alleged persecution of Hindus in Bangladesh, arguing the country was founded on religious rather than linguistic grounds. He said Bengali Hindus are facing violence because India's post-Partition leadership failed to secure religious minorities' protection. The comments add to political tension between India's ruling party and Bangladesh's current government.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/hyderaba: Hyderabad police are investigating a hoax email warning of a 26/11 Mumbai-style attack, which named Kachiguda railway station and a nearby hotel as potential targets. No actual threat has been confirmed.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: Tamil Nadu's government has asked the Supreme Court to review its November 20 order permitting a one-time lighting of the 'Karthigai Deepam' lamp at a disputed stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai. The state's Hindu religious affairs department filed the petition a day after the court's interim order, which also stayed a Madras High Court ruling but said it created no lasting right to perform the ritual there.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/f: India's food safety regulator FSSAI has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International after a sample of its packaged drinking water was found unsafe, violating permitted bromate limits. A second lab test, requested by the company on appeal, also found unsafe levels of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons. The findings clear the way for legal action under the Food Safety and Standards Act.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/rahul-ga: Rahul Gandhi has reportedly endorsed maintaining strong India-Israel ties, citing India's defence needs and national interest, creating a rift with Congress allies over the party's stance on Israel's actions in Gaza and Palestine.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: Delhi's private schools are set to release their 100-point nursery admission criteria for the 2027-28 academic year, with applications opening December 1. The education department has outlined a detailed schedule, with seat-allotment lists due December 20 and February 2, and listed 62 criteria schools cannot use, such as parents' qualifications or interviews. The process concludes March 12.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/ban: More than 350 people in Karnataka have appealed after their names were deleted from the final electoral rolls following a Special Intensive Revision, despite having completed the required verification process. Some voters in Bengaluru told The Hindu that officials urged them to withdraw their appeals and reapply via Form 6 instead, or even filed the form on their behalf. Most appeals remain pending with election authorities.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/bag-with: A bag containing gold jewellery worth Rs 55 lakh, which went missing near a baggage scanner at Delhi's ISBT Kashmiri Gate terminal on November 12 after being swapped, has been recovered from Bengaluru.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: India's Enforcement Directorate has sent the UAE an extradition request for Ravi Uppal, co-founder of the Mahadev betting app, following his arrest there, and plans similar requests for two more accused, Shubham Soni and Anil Kumar Agarwal. They are linked to the Rs 6,000 crore online gambling syndicate, whose main promoter, Sourabh Chandrakar, was returned from Oman three weeks ago. Another accused, Vikash Chhaparia, is also detained in the UAE.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: Marico has fined independent director Bhaskar Bhat Rs 3 lakh after his spouse, Vrunda Bhaskar, bought 200 shares worth Rs 1.79 lakh during a restricted trading period on November 8. The company disclosed the penalty in a regulatory filing, noting it takes trading-window violations seriously.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: Logistics-tech firm FarEye says its AI platform helped Flipkart Wholesale, the e-commerce giant's B2B cash-and-carry arm, cut logistics costs by 6% and vehicle deployment by 8%, while reducing vehicle idle time by 10%. The gains came from digitizing dispatch, routing and compliance across a network handling over 200,000 orders monthly. It shows how Indian logistics firms are using AI to squeeze efficiency from supply chains amid thin e-commerce margins.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/: Foundation Future Industries, a San Francisco robotics startup building humanoid robots for defense and industrial use, has terminated employee health benefits after missing its October payroll amid a cash crunch. Workers will be offered COBRA coverage to pay for insurance themselves. The startup, founded in 2024 by Sankaet Pathak with Eric Trump as an investor and strategy advisor, highlights funding troubles hitting even well-connected robotics ventures.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: A World Bank report finds nearly 50 crore Indians moved out of poverty between 2011 and 2023, crediting government health programs, direct cash transfers and women's self-help groups. Continued infrastructure investment is seen as key to sustaining these gains and avoiding people slipping back into poverty. The findings feed into India's broader goal of becoming a developed economy, 'Viksit Bharat,' by 2047.
items.https://www.livemint.com/market/treasury: US Treasury futures fell in Asian trading on Monday as demand for safe havens eased on signs equities might be stabilizing after a sharp sell-off driven by unwinding AI-related trades. Asian regulators moved to curb the stock rout with measures like tighter short-selling limits and looser margin rules. Analysts noted bonds and stocks are again moving in opposite directions as investors weigh a possible rebound against sticky inflation and US fiscal worries.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6jr: Centrica (British Gas owner) chief Chris O'Shea said he is 'hugely concerned' that more people won't be able to pay energy bills when the UK's price cap rises in January, a jump forecast at £443 a year per household. The government's planned £100 in support was called a 'drop in the ocean' by Citizens Advice. O'Shea noted the first quarter sees the heaviest energy use, coinciding with Christmas costs.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: Tata Steel's board has approved selling its steel tubes and pipes business to APL Apollo Tubes for Rs 11,700 crore, along with its entire stake in Tata Steel Colors for Rs 16,300 crore, a combined Rs 28,000 crore deal. The operations will transfer to APL Apollo as a slump sale, letting Tata Steel focus on its core steelmaking business while APL Apollo expands its downstream product range.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: Tata Steel will transfer its tubes business and divest its stake in Tata Steel Colors to APL Apollo Tubes for a combined Rs 28,000 crore, pending regulatory approval. Tata Steel says APL Apollo's distribution network should help the tubes business grow further.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/: Tata Sons' board will discuss convening a special shareholder meeting (EGM) even though it currently lacks the quorum needed to hold one, according to the agenda for its latest meeting. The agenda also revisits Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata's objections to September's board proceedings and the group's loss-making businesses. Tata Trusts, the controlling shareholder, is seeking legal advice, with one executive suggesting the EGM may relate to extending chairman N. Chandrasekaran's term.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: India and the EU are expected to sign their long-awaited free trade agreement on December 16, a deal that would give 93% of Indian exports duty-free access to the EU market while making European luxury cars and wine cheaper in India. Together, the two economies account for a quarter of global GDP and about a third of world trade, valued at $11 trillion of the $33 trillion total.
items.https://inc42.com/features/fintech-stock: India's plan to levy a merchant discount rate (MDR) on some UPI transactions, long awaited by fintech firms as a new revenue stream, has been pushed back, possibly to 2027. Shares of Paytm, Pine Labs and MobiKwik fell sharply over the past week as a result, with Paytm down nearly 11%. The delay adds uncertainty to upcoming fintech IPO valuations that had priced in UPI monetization.
items.https://entrackr.com/report/weekly-fundi: Indian startups raised $290 million across 23 deals in the week of November 16-21, a sharp jump from $31.3 million the previous week. Growth-stage deals totaled $290 million including AI-CRM startup Dreamteam's $53 million round and fashion retailer Nexon Omniverse's roughly $52 million raise. Early-stage startups raised $147.7 million, led by Humyn Labs' $47 million Series A, alongside several new executive hires and two exits.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Chinese national Li Ming has been charged in Singapore with fraud over alleged transshipment of Nvidia chips. He was linked to Megaspeed, a company connected to Alice Huang, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's former romantic partner.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/vinfast-to-build-: Vietnamese EV maker VinFast is setting up a dedicated electric two-wheeler assembly line at its Thoothukudi plant in Tamil Nadu, built on an additional 500 acres secured under an earlier state MoU. The company's Asia CEO Tapan Ghosh said the first scooters should roll out early next year. The scooter line will run independently of VinFast's existing car assembly operations at the site.
items.https://entrackr.com/fintrackr/rooters-r: Gaming livestreaming platform Rooter more than doubled its revenue to Rs 170.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 78.9 crore a year earlier, while narrowing losses by 40% to Rs 19.2 crore. The company, founded in 2016, lets users stream games like BGMI and also sells in-game currency and gift cards as a second revenue stream. The results reflect growing monetization in India's expanding gaming and esports market.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Karnataka transport minister Byrathi Suresh said a final decision on bike taxis will follow discussions with the Advocate General, after a Supreme Court order on the matter. He said the state may frame regulations and restrictions rather than impose an outright ban.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: Mohammad Nawaz's all-round performance helped Pakistan A beat India A, chasing down a competitive target of 314, despite India slipping to 129 for 6 even with Tilak Varma scoring a century.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art: Mauricio Pochettino's first match as Manchester United manager ended in a chastening 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, with defender Leny Yoro sent off in the eighth minute to leave United down to 10 men. The result leaves United 19th in the 20-team Premier League after 11 games. It's a jarring start for Pochettino, who took the job just days after leaving his role coaching the United States national team.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/i: India kept alive hopes of a rare Test win in New Zealand on the final day in Wellington, with Washington Sundar and Prasidh Krishna taking two wickets to leave New Zealand at 157 for 4 at lunch. The hosts were still 195 runs short of erasing India's first-innings deficit, with eight wickets in hand. Jasprit Bumrah was used in short bursts as India pressed for a breakthrough.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: South Africa's Aiden Markram described stepping in as captain for the injured Temba Bavuma as 'quite a smooth transition,' adding he is eager to convert his good starts into big scores.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art: Liverpool's 18-year-old winger Rio Ngumoha was praised by pundit Danny Murphy as a 'wow' player after setting up a goal and scoring himself in Liverpool's 4-0 win over Manchester United. Murphy said Ngumoha's fearless, one-on-one style makes him hard to stop, even though his youth means he can still be inconsistent. The performance marks him as an emerging game-changer for Liverpool this season.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/tennis/al: Carlos Alcaraz beat world number one Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6(7) to win his first ATP Finals title in Turin, extending his winning streak to 14 matches and capturing his third straight title after Vienna and Paris. The Spaniard, the youngest man to complete a career Grand Slam, had finished runner-up at the Finals last year. He's gone 22-1 since a US Open quarter-final loss.
items.https://www.theverge.com/tech/1039851/ma: A string of major outages in the past week — a nationwide FAA ground stop, a multi-day Outlook disruption and a JPMorgan Chase banking outage — has prompted warnings that more are coming. US intelligence director Jay Clayton and Microsoft president Brad Smith both said rapid technological change, including the AI buildout, will keep causing system failures. They called for heavier investment in cybersecurity and infrastructure resilience to cope.
items.https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/11/googl: Google has rolled out a redesigned search homepage that drops the traditional search button in favor of buttons for AI features like image generation, file analysis and Gemini-powered brainstorming. The 'I'm Feeling Lucky' button remains. The change, confirmed by search VP Robby Stein, reflects how quickly Google is reshaping its core search product around AI tools even on its most basic page.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: AI safety research group METR has updated its widely cited 'time horizon' chart tracking how long a task AI models can complete, which previously showed that length doubling every four months. The new version adds longer and more open-ended tasks and finds models are improving steadily but are notably weaker at tasks requiring judgment than at coding. The update complicates simple narratives about AI capability growth.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/openai: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki proposed using 'perplexity,' a measure of how well a model predicts text, as a way to set speed limits on AI development, since capability benchmarks quickly become outdated. The idea follows Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's call to 'pace the frontier' with shared safety standards, after Anthropic's IPO filing warned of possible catastrophic risks. OpenAI's Sam Altman called the post one of the company's most important publications.
items.https://www.theverge.com/games/1039770/b: The game Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus has been review-bombed on Steam after players discovered AI-generated music, traced to Suno metadata, in one of its segments. Creator Edmund McMillen said he had no idea AI music was used and apologized. Valve requires developers to disclose AI use, but studio Nicalis reportedly never mentioned it, raising questions about compliance and transparency in game development.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: MIT Technology Review's AI Hype Index catalogs how pervasive AI has become, from Google's ad-revenue-costing AI Overviews to humanoid robots doing chores, an AI-linked cyberattack that disabled a supermarket's ice cream freezers, and Elon Musk's AI-narrated version of The Odyssey. The piece notes it's been ten years since AlphaGo beat Go champion Lee Sedol, using that milestone to frame how far — and how oddly — AI has spread since.
items.https://www.theverge.com/column/1039139/: People are increasingly using AI coding tools like Claude Code and Codex to hack and improve their own gadgets, such as removing ads and interface clutter from smart TVs. One developer in India described fixing his ad-heavy Xiaomi Android TV this way almost on a whim. The trend is fueling a growing market for developer-friendly hardware and software tweaks across consumer electronics.
items.https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/11: Security researcher HD Moore planted 2 million trackable fake secrets, including AWS access keys, into prompts sent through AI 'router' services like OpenRouter and Vercel to test if sensitive data leaks. The experiment found the AI supply chain, where brokers route prompts to the cheapest or best-suited inference provider, leaks sensitive information extensively. It highlights a growing privacy risk as more apps route AI requests through third-party brokers instead of major providers directly.
items.https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/11/meta-: Meta is reconsidering its 2030 net-zero emissions goal after reporting the largest percentage increase in greenhouse gas emissions among major tech companies, driven by its AI data center buildout. The company's latest sustainability report said demand for AI infrastructure grew faster than almost anyone expected, forcing it to re-evaluate timelines and near-term targets. It signals growing tension between the AI boom and corporate climate commitments across the tech industry.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/why-da: Journalist Paris Marx's new book 'Hyperscale' argues that AI data centers have become a flashpoint for public anger at Big Tech, partly fueling backlash seen in recent midterm elections. Marx calls the data center buildout 'fundamentally unsustainable' and says the facilities are an easy target because their impact — on power bills and local communities — is tangible and physical, regardless of people's politics.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/21/a-tale: Nvidia posted strong earnings and insists ousted CEO Jensen Huang won't return, even as some tech executives and investors publicly campaign for his reinstatement. Interim CEO Colette Kress also confirmed Nvidia will stop selling its H200 chips in China. Despite the solid results, Nvidia's falling stock price suggests Wall Street isn't fully reassured by current leadership.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: A petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO has gathered over 115,000 signatures, including prominent figures from Hugging Face and venture firms Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital. Many signatories are tied to the open-source AI movement, which argues that concentrating AI power among a few large companies hurts everyone else. Critics note these backers also stand to profit if startups can build cheaply on open models instead of paying big AI labs.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/21/is-sel: Microdrama startup Shortical, known for bite-sized melodramatic soap operas, is increasingly using AI-generated content, including a new series starring an actor who licensed his face to the platform rather than appearing on camera. The approach, already common in China, cuts production costs sharply while offering high profit potential. It raises questions about whether AI face-licensing could become a wider trend in Hollywood-style entertainment.
items.https://www.theverge.com/tech/1039554/un: UN diplomats meeting in Geneva failed to agree on binding rules for autonomous weapons, or 'killer robots,' settling instead for a pledge to 'start discussing options.' The Red Cross had urged legally binding rules within a year, backed by the UN secretary-general and Pope Leo, but countries instead got two years to propose regulations, some of which may remain optional. Autonomous drones have already caused significant civilian deaths in Ukraine, Gaza and Sudan.
items.https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026: Four Black students at a Baltimore County school are suing after an AI gun-detection system mistook a Doritos bag for a weapon, triggering a police response with multiple patrol cars even after officials confirmed there was no threat. The lawsuit says the school system's AI alerts are false positives over 99% of the time. The case highlights risks of relying on unreliable AI surveillance in schools, especially for students of color.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/how-no: Early investors Notable Capital, GIC and Baillie Gifford explain why they bet big on Anthropic before its IPO, despite the AI lab trailing rivals like OpenAI at the time. Notable Capital put roughly 10% of its fund into Anthropic's Series E at a $61.5 billion valuation, its highest-ever bet, after finding developers were using Claude over ChatGPT 70% of the time. The piece shows how developer adoption data shaped major venture bets on AI labs.
items.https://www.theverge.com/podcast/1038701: A Verge podcast explores whether Anthropic, the AI company behind Claude, can keep prioritizing safety now that it has gone public on the Nasdaq. The company faces pressure to keep growing revenue to cover compute costs estimated at roughly $900 billion over the coming years, all while maintaining its safety-focused mission. It captures the tension between an AI safety mandate and the demands of being a public company.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/bewakoof-cofounde: Prabhkiran Singh, former CEO of fashion brand Bewakoof, has launched Save8, an AI-powered shopping assistant that compares prices and deals across more than 1,000 online and quick-commerce stores. The launch marks his return to entrepreneurship months after exiting Bewakoof, which he led for nearly 14 years. Singh is also in fundraising talks with investors including All In Capital, though terms remain undisclosed.
items.https://inc42.com/features/sarvams-token: Bengaluru startup Sarvam AI has launched Token Factory, a platform letting developers access multiple AI models via API and pay only for tokens used, without managing GPU infrastructure themselves. The launch intensifies competition in India's emerging AI inference market, where players like L&T, E2E Networks' Jarvislabs and Utho Labs are also building similar offerings. It reflects a shift among Indian infrastructure firms from simple GPU rentals toward managed, usage-based AI services.
